title: Espagnole Sauce (Brown Sauce)
description: One of the five classic French mother sauces, made with a brown roux, mirepoix, tomato purée, and rich brown stock to create a deep, robust foundation for demi-glace and many traditional meat sauces.

ingredients.title: For the Espagnole Sauce
items: Brown stock (veal or beef) – 500 ml (2 cups)
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Brown Roux
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and whisk continuously until a deep golden-brown roux forms.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Flavor Base
steps: Add the diced carrot, onion, and celery, then sauté until lightly caramelized.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2–3 minutes to deepen the flavor and reduce its acidity.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Simmering the Sauce
steps: Gradually whisk in the hot brown stock until smooth and well combined.
Add the bouquet garni and bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 45–60 minutes, skimming any impurities from the surface as needed.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Finishing
steps: Strain the sauce through a fine sieve or chinois for a smooth finish.
Adjust seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper before serving.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with roasted or grilled beef, lamb, or veal.
Use as the base for Demi-Glace, Bordelaise, and Chasseur sauces.
Pair with braised meats and hearty stews.
Drizzle over steaks, meatloaf, or roasted vegetables for added richness.

chefTips: Caramelize both the roux and mirepoix properly to develop a rich, complex flavor.
Use high-quality homemade brown stock for the most authentic taste.
Simmer gently rather than boiling to maintain a smooth, velvety texture.
Skim impurities regularly during cooking for a cleaner, more refined sauce.
Espagnole is one of the five classic French mother sauces and the essential base for demi-glace.
